title: Phase 8: Background jobs and message processing
description: Offload long-running work (OCR receipt processing, accounting exports, email notifications) from the request path using MassTransit with the outbox pattern. Implement retry, dead-letter, and idempotency guarantees.

data.text: Some work must not block the user's HTTP request: OCR scanning a receipt image, exporting thousands of expense rows to CSV, or sending a notification email. These operations should be reliable, retryable, and idempotent. In this phase, you'll use MassTransit + RabbitMQ for message routing and the transactional outbox to guarantee delivery.

data.title: Benefits
items: Decouples the API from downstream consumers (OCR service, email provider, accounting export).
Retries automatically on transient failures without user intervention.
Dead-letter queue isolates poison messages without crashing the consumer.
Outbox pattern guarantees exactly-once publishing even after database rollbacks.

data.caption: Message flow: API → Outbox → RabbitMQ → Consumers
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as MediatR Handler
    participant D as ExpenseDbContext
    participant O as Outbox Service
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant C1 as ReceiptOcrConsumer
    participant C2 as NotificationConsumer
    participant C3 as AccountingExportConsumer

    H->>D: Save expense report + domain events
    D->>O: Move events to Outbox table (same transaction)
    O->>MQ: Publish events (background worker)
    MQ->>C1: ReceiptUploaded
    MQ->>C2: ExpenseReportApproved
    MQ->>C3: ExpenseReportPaid

    Note over O,MQ: If worker crashes, outbox retries on next poll. No message is lost.

data.text: The outbox is the single most important reliability pattern in distributed systems. Without it, your handler might persist the ExpenseReport but crash before publishing the event — leaving the database updated but no downstream side effect triggered.

data.title: C#: Outbox message entity and EF Core interceptor
data.content: An EF Core SaveChangesInterceptor atomically saves domain events into the Outbox table alongside the aggregate.

data.text: Consumers are lightweight, focused classes that handle one message type. They receive messages from RabbitMQ queues and perform the actual side effect.

data.title: C#: ReceiptOcrConsumer using MassTransit
data.content: Consume ReceiptUploaded, send image to OCR service, persist extracted fields back to the database.

data.text: RabbitMQ guarantees at-least-once delivery. If your consumer crashes after processing but before acknowledging, the message is redelivered. Use message IDs or natural keys to make handlers idempotent.

data.title: C#: Idempotent handler using message ID
data.content: Skip processing if the message was already handled.

data.title: MassTransit retry policy
data.text: Configure retry with exponential backoff: immediate (3x), then 1s, 5s, 30s. Use a dead-letter queue for messages that exhaust retries. Monitor the DLQ — a growing queue signals a bug or an external outage.

data.title: C#: MassTransit configuration with outbox and retry
data.content: Use the built-in Entity Framework Core outbox for reliable publishing.

items.text: RabbitMQ running locally (Docker Compose) with MassTransit configured.
Outbox interceptor moves domain events to Outbox table in the same transaction.
Background worker publishes outbox messages to RabbitMQ every 10 seconds.
ReceiptOcrConsumer processes receipts with retry and exponential backoff.
All consumers are idempotent (checked via message ID or natural key).
Dead-letter queue alerts are wired to a monitoring channel.

data.title: Phase 8 summary
points: Outbox pattern guarantees event delivery without dual-write hazards.
MassTransis consumers are focused, retryable, and idempotent.
DLQ isolates poison messages without crashing the consumer.
Background jobs keep the HTTP request path under 200ms.
data.takeaway: Reliability is built in layers: the outbox protects against crashes, retry handles transient failures, idempotency handles redeliveries, and the DLQ handles permanent failures.
